overrideReason: All 3 automated attempts failed identically with '0/6 - not judged, a cheaper layer already failed'. Investigated rather than assuming a repeat of an already-fixed environment issue: the implementer's own diff added `--basetemp=.pytest-tmp` to pyproject.toml's addopts - a change entirely out of this story's declared scope (touches: supabase/migrations/, ingest/persist.py, tests/test_persist.py only). That change overrides .uf/config.json's existing TEMP/TMP env-var fix from PRD-012 (which handles pytest's OS-level temp housekeeping), forcing pytest back onto a project-relative directory whose own ACL became unreclaimable after repeated attempt runs - the identical PermissionError/WinError 5 class already logged as a durable lesson, recurring because this specific out-of-scope change silently defeated the existing fix. Reverted pyproject.toml's addopts to its pre-story state (no --basetemp override, letting .uf/config.json's TEMP/TMP env override govern pytest's temp root as designed). Verified clean with the fix reverted: `uv run mypy ingest --strict` and `uv run ruff check` both clean, and the exact gate command (`.uf/config.json`'s 'test' gate, reproduced directly) plus a manual `uv run pytest -q -m "not integration"` with TEMP/TMP set both pass 292/292 offline tests with zero errors. Separately verified the story's own actual content (the migration file, persist.py's changes, and the new tests in test_persist.py) by direct code review - all six criteria are genuinely, correctly implemented; the only defect was the accidental, out-of-scope pyproject.toml regression, not the migration/persist logic itself.

results.note: supabase/migrations/20260927120000_add_datapoint_reference_period_and_published_at.sql adds `reference_period text` and `published_at timestamptz` to public.datapoints, both nullable (no NOT NULL constraint), and recreates datapoints_read/board_read views to include both columns. tests/test_persist.py::test_migration_adds_nullable_reference_period_and_published_at_columns asserts this directly against the real migration file text.

Both new columns are added without a default, so every pre-existing row reads NULL for both. No existing column, view, or persist_datapoint call signature was removed or renamed - confirmed by direct diff review of ingest/persist.py, which only adds two new optional trailing parameters.

persist_datapoint(..., reference_period: str | None = None, published_at: datetime | None = None) accepts and writes both fields on insert and update; tests/test_persist.py has both an offline (mocked connection) and a live-database integration test confirming the write path (test_existing_call_pattern_writes_null_reference_period_and_published_at_offline and its live counterpart at line 318).

Every existing fetcher's call pattern (no reference_period/published_at arguments) continues to work unchanged - both parameters default to None. Confirmed by the same tests as C3, which explicitly call persist_datapoint using the pre-existing signature and assert both new columns write NULL.

test_reference_period_and_published_at_are_independently_nullable_offline (and its live-database counterpart at line 369) directly tests a row with one field set and the other None, in both directions.

`uv run pytest -q -m "not integration"` re-run fresh against current HEAD, with the pyproject.toml regression reverted: 292 passed, 52 deselected, exit 0 - confirmed both via direct invocation and by reproducing .uf/config.json's own 'test' gate command exactly.
